note: Literature reports cases of PLAA mutations presenting with cerebral atrophy where cerebellar atrophy was lacking or delayed, supporting differential temporal onset.

evidence.text: In a cohort screening of PEHO and PEHO-like syndromes, patients harboring pathogenic variants in PLAA exhibited generalized cerebral atrophy but were classified as PEHO-like specifically because cerebellar atrophy was lacking.

source.title: PEHO syndrome: the endpoint of different genetic epilepsies
source.quote: generalised cerebral atrophy.6 They met the same ... like syndrome because cerebellar atrophy was lacking. ... pathogenic variant in the gene PLAA; c.68G>T p.

evidence.text: Loss of PLAA causes lethal infantile epileptic encephalopathy characterized by both progressive microcephaly and progressive cerebral and cerebellar volume loss.

source.title: PLAA mutations cause a lethal infantile epileptic encephalopathy by disrupting ubiquitin-mediated endolysosomal degradation of synaptic proteins
source.quote: features of cerebellar and cerebral atrophy. Autozygosity … birth and around a year highlight progressive microcephaly.
